output:
I'll start by looking at the docs and package layout.

The last call was malformed and didn't run. I've read all the code and docs, and I'm now applying the fixes.

I'll use the edit tool, one file at a time, starting with the lexer.

Now the loader: keep the including file's section after an include, list each shared file once, and read a whole file before applying its includes.

Unit tests pass. Next I'll run the repo's check tool and a full `run` on the data directory.

Every expected document matches. Now I'll run `tools/check.py` and some edge cases against the docs.

That error is correct, because `${x}` isn't in section `a`. I'll fix my test input and rerun.

I fixed the bugs in `layercfg`, and the 56 unit tests now pass. I ran `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` and it exited OK.

I also ran `python -m layercfg run` on `/app/data`. All 136 resolved documents match `tests/expected/resolved`. `tools/check.py` reports 0 broken on every rule, and it lists 14 configs the package refuses. I also ran one made-up config covering quoting, `$$`, dotted sections, templates, includes and `get`, and the output matched the docs.

The fixes, by file:
- **`lexer.py`:**
  - The separator is now whichever of `=` or `:` comes first.
  - Section and include lines accept only spaces and tabs as whitespace, not other whitespace such as form feeds.
- **`values.py`:**
  - An inline `#` starts a comment only after a space or tab. `color=#336699` keeps its value.
  - `\$` becomes `$$`, so `"\${HOME}"` stays as the text `${HOME}`.
  - Only spaces and tabs are stripped.
- **`loader.py`:**
  - After an include, the including file stays in the section it was in. Before, it picked up the shared file's last section.
  - Each shared file is listed once, in first-read order.
  - A file is read in full, including its values, before any of its includes run.
- **`interp.py`:**
  - References are no longer expanded while the config is merged. They are expanded afterwards, so they see each key's final value, and `path = ${path}:/opt/bin` is a cycle.
  - A dotted reference like `${db.replica.host}` splits at the last dot.
- **`report.py`:** template sections (names starting with `_`) are no longer written.
- **`convert.py`:**
  - `ms` now parses as a duration unit. Before, `5ms` was rejected.
  - `KB`, `MB`, `GB` and `TB` are powers of 1000.
  - List items drop empty entries.
  - Whitespace stripping is limited to spaces and tabs.
- **`data.py`:** files are read as bytes and decoded as UTF-8, so a lone `\r` isn't turned into a line break.

I did not touch `/app/tests`, `/app/data` or `/app/docs`. `/app/STATUS.json` says `success`.

command_result.command: cd /app && find . -path ./.git -prune -o -type f -print | head -100 && cat docs/overview.md && wc -l layercfg/*.py docs/*
cd /app && cat docs/syntax.md docs/include.md docs/interp.md docs/types.md docs/output.md docs/changelog.md; ls docs/archive tools 2>&1
cd /app && for f in layercfg/*.py; do echo "=== $f"; cat $f; done
cd /app && sed -n 40,70p docs/include.md; cat docs/interp.md; cat layercfg/interp.py; sed -n 1,35p layercfg/lexer.py

cd /app && python - <<'EOF'
import re
p='layercfg/convert.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('(d|h|m|s|ms)")','(ms|d|h|m|s)")')
s=s.replace('"KB": 1024, "MB": 1024 ** 2, "GB": 1024 ** 3, "TB": 1024 ** 4,','"KB": 1000, "MB": 1000 ** 2, "GB": 1000 ** 3, "TB": 1000 ** 4,')
s=s.replace('''    items = [item.strip() for item in text.split(",")]
    return items if text else []''','''    items = [item.strip(" \\t") for item in text.split(",")]
    return [item for item in items if item]''')
s=s.replace('CONVERTERS[type_name](text.strip())','CONVERTERS[type_name](text.strip(" \\t"))')
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='layercfg/data.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")','path.read_bytes().decode("utf-8")')
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='layercfg/interp.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''        if a.interp:
            a = Assignment(a.section, a.key, Resolver(store).expand(a.section, a.text, (), a.where), False, a.where)
''','')
s=s.replace('name.split(".", 1)','name.rsplit(".", 1)')
open(p,'w').write(s)

p='layercfg/report.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('for section in sorted(store):\n','for section in sorted(store):\n        if not written(section):\n            continue\n')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
git diff --stat 2>&1 | tail -3; grep -n 'strip\|ms|\|1000' layercfg/convert.py

cd /app && python - <<'EOF'
p='layercfg/loader.py'
s=open(p).read()
old=s[s.index('        for line in lines:'):s.index('    def _include')]
new='''        parsed = []
        for line in lines:
            where = f"{label} line {line.lineno}"
            if line.kind == "assign":
                value, interp = parse_value(line.value, where)
                parsed.append((line, where, value, interp))
            else:
                parsed.append((line, where, None, False))
        for line, where, value, interp in parsed:
            if line.kind == "section":
                section = line.name
            elif line.kind == "include":
                self._include(line.name, where)
            else:
                self.assignments.append(Assignment(section, line.name, value, interp, where))
        self._stack.pop()
        return section

'''
s=s.replace(old,new)
s=s.replace('''        self.includes.append(name)
        return self._file(name, text)''','''        if name in self._stack:
            raise IncludeError(f"{where}: {name} includes itself through {' -> '.join(self._stack)}")
        if name not in self.includes:
            self.includes.append(name)
        self._file(name, text)''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
sed -n 28,70p layercfg/loader.py; python -m unittest discover -s tests -t . 2>&1 | tail -30

cd /app && sed -n 1,30p tools/check.py | head -40; python tools/check.py --help 2>&1 | head; rm -rf /tmp/out; python -m layercfg run --out /tmp/out; echo $?; ls /tmp/out/resolved | wc -l; cat /tmp/out/errors.json | head -60; for f in tests/expected/resolved/*.json; do cmp -s $f /tmp/out/resolved/$(basename $f) || echo DIFF $f; done

cd /app && python tools/check.py; mkdir -p /tmp/d/configs /tmp/d/shared && cd /tmp/d && echo '{"types":{"a.n":"int","a.s":"size","a.d":"duration","*.l":"list"}}' > schema.json && printf 'x = 1
[A]
n = 0x1_f
s = 1.5 KB
d = 1s500ms
l = a, b,, c ,
q = "\${HOME} \$5" # c
t = $$${x} cost $5
u = ${main.x}${defaults.z}
c=#33 
[defaults]
z=Z
[_t]
k=1
[a.b]
r=${_t.k}${a.n}
%%include s.conf
y: p=q#r
' > configs/e.conf && printf '[other]
v=1
' > shared/s.conf && cd /app && python -m layercfg resolve e --data /tmp/d

cd /tmp/d && sed -i 's/\$\$\${x}/$$${main.x}/' configs/e.conf && cd /app && python -m layercfg resolve e --data /tmp/d; python -m layercfg get e a.n --data /tmp/d; python -m layercfg get e a.b.r --data /tmp/d
